page_summary: Evaluation table of the 2021-2023 CHIP: the hospital's progress on mental health and substance use strategies (peer support, recovery events, virtual IOP, co-response with law enforcement).
Evaluation table continued: healthy lifestyle and barriers-to-access strategies with the hospital's progress (pregnancy center partnership, childcare, campus expansion, workforce).
Evaluation table continued (workforce pipeline, specialty providers, SDOH outreach), then prose on how the next CHIP will address needs.
Key informant interview synthesis on behavioral health: substance use, mental health, suicide, affordability, and workforce, with verbatim informant quotes.
Key informant themes on social connection and the lack of affordable childcare; almost nothing on this page fits the codebook.

Community resource directory: the end of a public health clinic's service list, Connecting Ties, and Valdez Food Bank. These are other organizations' services; no hospital action or priority is stated on this page, so no rows.
Describes the prioritization process and criteria, then begins Table 1 (behavioral health strategies).

Strategy tables: end of the behavioral health table (suicide response) and the basic needs / economic security table (charity care, Medicaid applications, housing and childcare collaboration), plus resource commitment and partners.
End of the partner list for the previous priority, then Table 3 (physical health): primary care provider recruitment, chronic disease education, preventive care.
